source_evidence.anchor: Theorem 2.8.1 proof paragraph immediately preceding Equation (2.23)
source_evidence.observation: The proof defines S = sum_{i=1}^N X_i and says to multiply S ≥ t by a parameter λ, exponentiate, and use Markov's inequality and independence, leading to the bound previously numbered (2.7).

The displayed equation is P{S ≥ t} ≤ e^{-λt} product_{i=1}^N E exp(λX_i). It is a one-sided upper-tail estimate, has no absolute value and no prefactor 2, and factors the MGF into one factor per summand.

source_evidence.anchor: Equation (2.7) and the sentence following its subsequent substitution
source_evidence.observation: The earlier Chernoff argument gives the same Markov-and-independence product bound and explicitly states that it holds for any λ > 0. Equation (2.23) invokes this bound by number.
The inherited setting consists of independent, mean-zero, sub-exponential random variables X_1,...,X_N and a threshold t ≥ 0.

binders: N is the implicitly positive integer number of summands (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Theorem 2.8.1 statement).
X_1,...,X_N are real random variables on a common implicit probability space (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Theorem 2.8.1 statement and proof).
S abbreviates sum_{i=1}^N X_i (PDF page 25/printed page 36, opening proof sentence).
t is the nonnegative real threshold inherited from Theorem 2.8.1 (PDF page 25/printed page 36, theorem statement).
λ is a positive real exponential-tilting parameter; positivity is inherited from the referenced Equation (2.7) argument (PDF page 8/printed page 19, sentence stating the bound holds for any λ > 0).
hypotheses: X_1,...,X_N are jointly independent (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Theorem 2.8.1 statement and the proof's explicit use of independence).

The enclosing theorem also assumes every X_i is mean zero and sub-exponential, although those properties are not used in the Markov-and-factorization step itself (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Theorem 2.8.1 statement).
λ > 0 (PDF page 8/printed page 19, the Equation (2.7) argument expressly stating its range).
conclusions: P{S ≥ t} ≤ exp(-λt) product_{i=1}^N E exp(λX_i) (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.23)).
definitions_and_conventions: S = sum_{i=1}^N X_i (PDF page 25/printed page 36, opening proof sentence).
E exp(λX_i) is the moment generating function of X_i at λ (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.23) and the following paragraph).
The product ranges over every index i = 1,...,N and arises from independence (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.23) and its introducing sentence).
The left event is the one-sided event S ≥ t, not the two-sided event |S| ≥ t (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.23)).
implicit_context: The inequality is the exponential Markov bound after multiplying S ≥ t by λ > 0 and exponentiating (PDF page 25/printed page 36, paragraph before Equation (2.23); PDF page 8/printed page 19, Equation (2.7) derivation).
Joint independence is used to replace E exp(λ sum_i X_i) by product_i E exp(λX_i) (PDF page 25/printed page 36, paragraph before Equation (2.23)).
The mean-zero and sub-exponential assumptions become relevant only in the next step, where each individual MGF is bounded (PDF page 25/printed page 36, paragraph following Equation (2.23)).

details: Equation (2.23) bounds only P{S ≥ t}; it contains no absolute value and no lower-tail event (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.23)).
The factor 2 appearing in the final theorem is absent from this intermediate upper-tail estimate (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.23) versus Theorem 2.8.1 statement).
The estimate is valid for each λ > 0, with t ≥ 0 inherited from the theorem (PDF page 8/printed page 19, Equation (2.7) discussion; PDF page 25/printed page 36, Theorem 2.8.1).
No optimization or small-λ restriction has yet been imposed at Equation (2.23); the small-λ constraint appears next as Equation (2.24) (PDF page 25/printed page 36).
The right side is exactly exp(-λt) times a product of N individual MGFs (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.23)).
Independence, rather than identical distribution, supplies the product; the X_i may have different laws (PDF page 25/printed page 36, theorem statement and proof).

undebatable_constraints: The left side is P{S ≥ t}, a one-sided non-strict upper-tail event, with S = sum_{i=1}^N X_i (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.23)).
The exponential prefactor is exactly exp(-λt) (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.23)).
The remaining right-hand factor is exactly product_{i=1}^N E exp(λX_i) (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.23)).
The parameter λ is positive, as inherited from the explicitly referenced Equation (2.7) argument (PDF page 8/printed page 19).
Independence is essential to the product factorization (PDF page 25/printed page 36, paragraph introducing Equation (2.23)).
There is no absolute value around S and no numeric prefactor 2 in Equation (2.23) (PDF page 25/printed page 36).

ambiguities.issue: Positivity of λ is not restated beside Equation (2.23)
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 25/printed page 36 calls λ only 'a parameter' and says the step leads to bound (2.7); PDF page 8/printed page 19 states that the referenced bound holds for any λ > 0.
ambiguities.impact: A standalone formalization of Equation (2.23) must retain λ > 0 from the cross-referenced derivation; allowing negative λ would reverse the event transformation.

ambiguities.issue: Possible infinite MGFs before the small-λ restriction
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 24/printed page 35 notes that a sub-exponential random variable may have an infinite MGF for large λ, while Equation (2.23) is displayed before Equation (2.24) restricts λ.
ambiguities.impact: The source appears to understand Equation (2.23) as an extended-valued or trivially valid bound when a product factor is infinite, but it does not specify the arithmetic convention.

ambiguities.issue: N is not explicitly quantified as positive
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 25/printed page 36 writes X_1,...,X_N and products and sums from 1 to N without a separate N ≥ 1 clause.
ambiguities.impact: A formalization must make the implicitly nonempty finite family explicit.

contracts.contract_plain_english: In the proof setting of independent, mean-zero, sub-exponential X_1,...,X_N, let S be their sum and let t ≥ 0. For every exponential-tilting parameter λ > 0, Markov's inequality followed by independence gives the one-sided bound P{S ≥ t} ≤ exp(-λt) product_{i=1}^N E exp(λX_i). This is exactly Equation (2.23) on PDF page 25/printed page 36; it is an intermediate upper-tail estimate and has neither an absolute value nor a prefactor 2.

source_evidence.observation: To bound each MGF, the proof invokes property e of Proposition 2.7.1 and says λ must be small enough.

The displayed sufficient restriction is |λ| ≤ c / max_i ||X_i||_{psi_1}, with a non-strict inequality, absolute value on λ, a lower-case absolute constant c in the numerator, and the maximum psi-one norm in the denominator.
Under the restriction, the proof states that E exp(λX_i) ≤ exp(C λ^2 ||X_i||_{psi_1}^2) for each term X_i.
For a mean-zero X, property e is E exp(λX) ≤ exp(K_5^2 λ^2) for all |λ| ≤ 1/K_5. Proposition 2.7.1 says its parameters differ by at most an absolute constant factor.

The source explains that property e holds for a K_5 within an absolute constant factor of ||X||_{psi_1}; this is the reason unspecified absolute constants c and C appear in the uniform restriction and MGF bound.
The sub-exponential norm is ||X||_{psi_1} = inf{s > 0 : E exp(|X|/s) ≤ 2}.

binders: N is the implicitly positive number of variables (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Theorem 2.8.1).
X_1,...,X_N are real random variables in the inherited Theorem 2.8.1 setting (PDF page 25/printed page 36).
λ is a real MGF parameter, allowed to have either sign because Equation (2.24) constrains |λ| (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.24)).

c and C denote positive absolute constants, independent of N, the X_i, i, and λ; their numerical values are unspecified (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.24), following sentence, and footnote 8).
hypotheses: Each X_i is mean zero and sub-exponential (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Theorem 2.8.1; PDF page 21/printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1 property e).
The enclosing theorem assumes the X_i are jointly independent, although independence is not needed for the individual MGF estimate itself (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Theorem 2.8.1).
conclusions: For every i = 1,...,N, E exp(λX_i) ≤ exp(C λ² ||X_i||_{psi_1}²) (PDF page 25/printed page 36, sentence immediately following Equation (2.24)).
definitions_and_conventions: ||X||_{psi_1} = inf{s > 0 : E exp(|X|/s) ≤ 2} (PDF page 22/printed page 33, Definition 2.7.5 and Equation (2.21)).
max_i ||X_i||_{psi_1} is the maximum individual sub-exponential norm over i = 1,...,N (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.24)).
Property e states that a mean-zero sub-exponential variable has a quadratic MGF bound for |λ| at most the reciprocal of an appropriate parameter K_5 (PDF page 21/printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1).
Footnote 8 permits replacement of K_5 by ||X_i||_{psi_1} at the cost of unspecified absolute constants c and C (PDF page 25/printed page 36).
implicit_context: Equation (2.24) is a sufficient uniform restriction ensuring property e can be applied simultaneously to every X_i (PDF page 25/printed page 36, paragraph surrounding Equation (2.24)).
The use of the maximum norm makes the same λ valid for all indices, even when the X_i have different norms (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.24) and following sentence).
Mean zero is essential for property e as stated; Proposition 2.7.1 adds property e only under the additional assumption E X = 0 (PDF page 21/printed page 32).
The MGF bounds are intended for substitution into the product in Equation (2.23) (PDF page 25/printed page 36, sentence following the individual MGF estimate).

details: The restriction is two-sided in λ because it uses |λ|, and equality at the boundary is permitted (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.24)).
The denominator is the maximum psi-one norm, not a sum, average, or norm of the vector of norms (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.24)).

The numerator c and exponent coefficient C are unspecified positive absolute constants arising from equivalence of sub-exponential parameters (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.24), following sentence, and footnote 8).
Neither c nor C may depend on N, i, the distribution of X_i, or λ (PDF page 21/printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1 absolute-constant-factor statement; PDF page 25/printed page 36, footnote 8).
The exponent is quadratic in λ and in ||X_i||_{psi_1}: C λ² ||X_i||_{psi_1}² (PDF page 25/printed page 36, sentence following Equation (2.24)).
The conclusion is an individual bound for each i, not yet a product or summed exponent (PDF page 25/printed page 36, sentence following Equation (2.24)).

undebatable_constraints: Equation (2.24) is |λ| ≤ c / max_i ||X_i||_{psi_1}, with absolute value on λ and a non-strict inequality (PDF page 25/printed page 36).
The denominator is exactly the maximum individual psi-one norm (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.24)).
The immediately following conclusion is E exp(λX_i) ≤ exp(C λ² ||X_i||_{psi_1}²) for each i (PDF page 25/printed page 36).
The exponent contains λ² and the square of the individual norm, not the maximum norm (PDF page 25/printed page 36, sentence following Equation (2.24)).
The constants c and C are positive absolute constants with unspecified numerical values (PDF page 21/printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1; PDF page 25/printed page 36, footnote 8).
Mean zero is required for the invoked property e (PDF page 21/printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1).
Equation (2.24) is a sufficient simultaneous small-λ condition, not an equivalence or a necessary condition (PDF page 25/printed page 36, wording 'if λ is small enough so that').

ambiguities.issue: The absolute constants c and C are not numerically fixed
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 25/printed page 36 uses c in Equation (2.24), C in the following MGF estimate, and footnote 8 says only that the relevant parameters are within an absolute constant factor.
ambiguities.impact: A formalization must existentially quantify suitable uniform constants or otherwise encode the book's flexible absolute-constant convention; it must not invent numeric values.

ambiguities.issue: The case max_i ||X_i||_{psi_1} = 0 is not defined
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 25/printed page 36 divides c by the maximum norm in Equation (2.24), and the enclosing theorem does not exclude all X_i being zero almost surely.
ambiguities.impact: A formalization must choose a zero-denominator convention, state a positive-maximum hypothesis, or separately handle the degenerate family.

ambiguities.issue: The source does not explicitly quantify 'for every i' in the following MGF sentence
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 25/printed page 36 says 'To bound the MGF of each term X_i' and then writes E exp(λX_i) ≤ exp(Cλ²||X_i||_{psi_1}²).
ambiguities.impact: The intended reading is a simultaneous bound for all i = 1,...,N, but a formalization should make that quantification explicit.

ambiguities.issue: N is not explicitly constrained to be positive
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 25/printed page 36 writes X_1,...,X_N and max_i without a separate N ≥ 1 clause.
ambiguities.impact: The maximum in Equation (2.24) requires an implicitly nonempty finite family.

contracts.contract_plain_english: In the mean-zero sub-exponential setting of Theorem 2.8.1, choose a real λ whose magnitude is at most an unspecified positive absolute constant c divided by the largest psi-one norm among X_1,...,X_N. Then property e of Proposition 2.7.1, together with absolute-constant equivalence of its parameter and the psi-one norm, gives for every i the bound E exp(λX_i) ≤ exp(C λ² ||X_i||_{psi_1}²), where C is another positive absolute constant. Equation (2.24) and this immediately following MGF-use sentence appear on PDF page 25/printed page 36.
